subject: Service reachability diversion — EU peering disruption & customer reroute instructions
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: alice.park@greenlineretail.com, infra@greenlineretail.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service reachability diversion — EU peering disruption & customer reroute instructions

Hi Alice / Greenline infra team,

I wanted to update you directly: we are seeing a peering disruption affecting a subset of our EU egress paths which can cause intermittent 502/timeout errors for workloads routed to eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Our network team has identified degraded exchange connectivity at a carrier POP and has implemented an automated diversion to alternate egress regions.

What you may observe right now:
- Short spikes of request failures (502 / connection reset) to the EU endpoints
- Increased p95 latency for sessions that remain pinned to the affected egress
- A small number of our routing rules have automatically migrated traffic to an EU fallback (with a different public egress IP set)

Immediate actions for Greenline (recommended, low-effort):
1) If you have hard-coded IP allowlists, add the fallback egress CIDR we posted on the incident page (https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-05-18-eu-peering) as a short-term permit.
2) Validate your health-checks against the alternate hostname: alternate-eu.redwood.ai (port 443).
3) If you run strict TLS SNI allowlists, ensure your routing accepts requests for alternate-eu.redwood.ai for the next 48 hours.

We're taking these steps internally:
- Network team (Markus) is coordinating with the carrier for an expedited repair.
- Traffic steering rules have been adjusted to reduce latency for latency-sensitive routes.
- We're preparing a targeted postmortem with timeline and mitigations.

I'll follow up with a short checklist you can run with your infra team (I've attached reachability-check-instructions.pdf). If you'd like us to perform a quick allowlist test from our side, reply with a good time window and we'll run one-minute test traffic to your endpoints.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts customer SLAs and we're treating it as priority P1.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachment: reachability-check-instructions.pdf (1 page — quick reachability tests and curl examples)
From: Alice Park <alice.park@greenlineretail.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@greenlineretail.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Service reachability diversion — EU peering disruption & customer reroute instructions

Thanks Grace — we saw the uptick in errors at 09:30 UTC. We do have IP allowlists (managed by our infra team). I've looped infra@ so they can action the CIDR add. Can your team confirm the exact egress CIDR(s) to add? Also, can you confirm there will be no TLS cert mismatch for alternate-eu.redwood.ai?

We're standing by to coordinate the short window for allowlist tests.

— Alice
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: infra@greenlineretail.com, alice.park@greenlineretail.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:05:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Service reachability diversion — EU peering disruption & customer reroute instructions

Hi Alice / Greenline infra team —

Short answers:
- Alternate egress CIDRs to add (temporary): 34.210.120.0/22, 34.211.16.0/21 (these are the NAT egress pools for alternate-eu).
- TLS: alternate-eu.redwood.ai is covered by our SAN certificate and will present the same certificate chain; there should be no TLS mismatch if you allow the hostname. We will, however, be using a different client egress IP set while the diversion is in place.

If you give us a 10-minute window in the next 30–60 minutes we can kick off a test from our monitoring probes to your health endpoint and confirm connectivity. Proposed window: 10:30–10:40 UTC. If that works, reply with your contact on the infra side and we'll run the test and paste results.

I'll also attach a short packet-capture checklist to the postmortem so you have the exact timings and AS paths we observed.

— Markus
Senior Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: alice.park@greenlineretail.com, infra@greenlineretail.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: post-incident status, action items, and draft postmortem link

Hi Alice / Greenline infra team —

Quick update now that the routing repair closed and we validated full carrier recovery. Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-05-18T08:55:00Z -> 2026-05-18T13:20:00Z (carrier POP degradation caused packet loss/HTTP 502s).
- Impact: Intermittent request failures and elevated p95 for customers pinned to the affected exchange; ~4% of EU-directed requests retried or failed during the window.
- Mitigation: Automated diversion to alternate-eu egress and temporary traffic steering decreased user-facing errors by ~85% after diversion.

Customer-facing actions completed:
- We posted the exact egress CIDRs you may need to add to allowlists in the incident page.
- We ran scheduled allowlist probes at 10:35 UTC and confirmed connectivity from alternate-eu address pool (results attached).

Next steps for Greenline (recommended):
- Confirm your security team has added 34.210.120.0/22 and 34.211.16.0/21 to allowlist for the next 72 hours.
- If you want an audit of your requests during the incident window, reply and we'll share a filtered access log slice (we can redact PII).
- Review the draft postmortem (link below) and flag any customer-specific questions you want included — we plan to publish a sanitized public postmortem later this week.

Draft postmortem: https://drive.redwood.ai/pm/INC-2026-05-18-eu-peering-draft (attachment: postmortem-draft-20260519.docx)
Incident timeline & probe results: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-05-18-eu-peering
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HS-12345

If it helps, Vanessa (CC) can join a 20-minute sync with your ops/security team to walk through the postmortem and the allowlist steps. Proposed windows: Wed 09:00–11:00 UTC or Wed 15:00–16:00 UTC. Let us know what works.

Thanks again for your patience — we appreciate the quick coordination.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: postmortem-draft-20260519.docx (3 pages — timeline and mitigation actions)
